types.name: Camera
types.doc:
Editor-side flying camera. Independent of CameraComponent (which is
the runtime/gameplay camera) — this drives the editor viewport and
has its own WASD/mouse controls. Projection mode + orthographic size
added for editor 2D / iso views; uses the same enum as
CameraComponent so the two stay in sync.

types.name: CameraControllerSystem
types.doc:
Drives the TransformComponent of every entity that owns a
CameraControllerComponent. Reads from an InputManager wired in via
SetInputManager() — typically EditorLayer (for PIE) and RuntimeLayer
hand over their input source. Without an InputManager the system
still runs the input-free modes (Follow, the target-tracking parts
of FirstPerson / TopDown) so non-input-driven behaviours survive
running the system in tooling contexts.

members.name: CameraCollisionSweep
members.signature: using CameraCollisionSweep = std::function<bool(const Vec3& from, const Vec3& to, float radius, uint32_t layerMask, float& outFraction)>
members.doc:
Spring-arm sweep for ThirdPersonOrbit collision, injected by the Game
tier (Scene) so the Camera module stays below Physics. Returns true
when the segment from `from` to `to`, swept with a sphere of
`radius` and filtered by `layerMask`, hits geometry — writing the
0..1 hit fraction to `outFraction`. Unset = no collision (full arm).

members.signature: virtual bool ModifyView(double realTimeSeconds, Vec3& pos, Vec3& forward, Vec3& up, float& fovDegrees) = 0
members.doc:
Mutate the evaluated view in place. realTimeSeconds is the engine's
real-time clock (a paused game still shakes, matching the blend
clock). Return false when finished — the system removes the modifier.

types.name: FCameraShake
types.doc:
Positional shake in the view plane (right/up axes) with a linear decay
envelope and two incommensurate frequencies per axis, so the motion never
settles into a visible loop. Optional fovPunch adds a degrees kick that
decays with the same envelope.

CameraSystem can fold them into the active view matrix.

members.name: GetMainCamera
members.doc: Get main camera (first camera with isMain=true, or first available)

members.name: ReelectMainCamera
members.doc:
Re-evaluate isMain flags over the registered list (cheap — does
not scan the world). Lets callers cache the registration pass
while still honoring runtime isMain flips.

members.name: SetViewTarget
members.doc:
View-target handover with a timed blend (the PlayerCameraManager
essential): the current evaluated view is captured as the FROM pose
and eased (smoothstep) into the new target's LIVE pose over
blendTimeSeconds. blendTime <= 0 cuts instantly. An invalid target
hands authority back to the elected main camera (with the same
blend). Retargeting mid-blend re-captures the blended pose, so
chained cuts stay continuous. Time source is the real-time clock —
a paused game can still blend its cameras.

members.name: PushViewTarget
members.doc:
View-target STACK on top of SetViewTarget — the cutscene/kill-cam
shape: Push hands authority to `target` remembering who had it, Pop
blends back to the remembered holder (or the elected main camera
when the stack empties / the remembered entity died with its world).
The stack stores TARGETS, not poses — a popped camera re-evaluates
live, so it may have moved while covered.

members.name: AddModifier
members.doc:
Camera modifiers — view mutators applied AFTER the blend on every
main-view evaluation. A modifier returning false is removed, so
one-shots (FCameraShake) clean themselves up.

members.signature: bool BuildSceneRendererCamera(Entity camEntity, float aspectRatio, SceneRendererCamera& out)
members.doc:
Build a SceneRendererCamera for an arbitrary camera entity. Used
by multi-camera setups that iterate every registered camera and
render each into its assigned viewport. Returns false if the
entity is invalid or lacks Camera + Transform components.

members.name: GetCamerasSortedByRenderOrder

List of camera entities sorted by CameraComponent::renderOrder
(ascending — earlier renderOrder is drawn first, later ones can
overdraw for PiP). Skips cameras whose component is disabled.

members.name: ClearWorld
members.doc:
Drop every registration that belongs to `world`. A registered Entity
holds a raw World*, so the registry MUST be purged before the world it
points at is destroyed — a scene unload, map travel or editor shutdown
otherwise leaves handles that read freed memory on the next lookup.

members.name: viewportX
members.doc:
Viewport region of the final output (normalized 0-1). Default
(0, 0, 1, 1) covers the whole output — the common single-camera
case. For split-screen left/right use (0, 0, 0.5, 1) and
(0.5, 0, 0.5, 1); for picture-in-picture put the inset camera at
something like (0.7, 0.7, 0.3, 0.3).

members.name: renderOrder
members.doc:
Render order — cameras are rendered low → high; later cameras
overdraw earlier ones in any overlapping viewport region. Useful
for PiP (background = order 0, inset = order 1) and for layering
UI-camera passes that share the same viewport.

members.name: Free
members.doc: WASD + mouse, like the editor flying camera — no target needed

members.name: FirstPerson
members.doc: Snap to followTarget + eyeOffset, mouse rotates view

members.name: ThirdPersonOrbit
members.doc: Orbit around followTarget at `distance`, mouse controls yaw/pitch

members.name: TopDown
members.doc: Hover above followTarget, looking down at `topDownPitch`

members.name: Follow
members.doc: Smoothly chase followTarget, no rotation control

types.name: CameraControllerComponent
types.doc:
Built-in camera controllers as a single component. Mode-irrelevant
fields are simply ignored by the system for the current mode — keeps
the inspector surface uniform without forcing five separate
component types for what's really a switch-on-enum.

CameraControllerSystem reads the active InputManager (wired in by
EditorLayer / RuntimeLayer) and writes back to TransformComponent
each frame. The CameraComponent on the same entity is untouched.

members.name: followTarget
members.doc:
Target entity for FirstPerson / ThirdPersonOrbit / TopDown /
Follow modes. INVALID_ENTITY (0) means "no target" — the system
falls back to Free behaviour for the modes that need a target so
gameplay code can wire the reference asynchronously.

members.name: eyeOffset
members.doc: FirstPerson: camera world position = followTarget.position + eyeOffset.

members.name: distance
members.doc:
ThirdPersonOrbit / TopDown: distance from target. In ThirdPersonOrbit
this is the spring-arm's full (unobstructed) length.

members.name: collisionEnabled
members.doc:
Spring-arm collision (ThirdPersonOrbit). When enabled the arm sweeps
from the pivot toward the desired camera position and pulls the
camera in to the first blocker, so it never clips through walls or
the floor. The sweep itself is injected by the Game tier
(CameraControllerSystem::SetCollisionSweep) because the Camera module
sits below Physics and can't query it directly.

members.name: probeRadius
members.doc:
Sphere-probe radius for the arm sweep (world units) — the camera is
kept this far off any blocking surface so the near plane can't poke
through it.

members.name: collisionLayerMask
members.doc:
Layers the arm collides with, as a bitmask over physics object
layers (bit N = layer N). Default clears the Player layer (bit 2) so
the arm never catches on the character it is framing.

members.name: collisionSmoothing
members.doc:
Arm retract/extend damping. The arm snaps IN instantly (never lets
the camera clip) but eases back OUT at rate 1 - exp(-s * dt) once the
blocker clears, so the camera doesn't pop back to full length.

members.name: minPitch
members.doc:
Orbit pitch clamp (radians). Engine convention: positive pitch
tips the camera up. Default range avoids the gimbal poles.

members.name: topDownPitch
members.doc:
TopDown: fixed pitch (looking down — negative tilts toward the
ground in our coordinate system).

members.name: followSmoothing
members.doc:
Follow smoothing — higher = snappier. Position is lerp'd with
factor `1 - exp(-smoothing * dt)` for framerate-independence.

members.name: requireMouseButton
members.doc:
UE-style: require right mouse button to be held before mouse
delta rotates the camera. Useful for editor/game hybrids.

members.name: lookSmoothing
members.doc:
Look smoothing — when > 0, current yaw/pitch lerp toward
targetYaw/targetPitch with rate `1 - exp(-lookSmoothing * dt)`.
0 disables (snap), 20-30 gives a cinematic feel, 50+ is barely
noticeable. Affects mouse and gamepad input uniformly.

members.name: gamepadLookSensitivity
members.doc:
Gamepad right-stick sensitivity — radians per second at full
deflection (stick=1.0). Mouse sensitivity is per-pixel and tiny
(0.002), gamepad needs much larger numbers because the stick is
held, not flicked.

members.name: gamepadDeadzone
members.doc:
Gamepad analog dead zone (0-1 stick magnitude). Below this the
stick is treated as centered — drift / resting-position twitch
doesn't rotate the camera.

members.name: yaw
members.doc:
Runtime — accumulated yaw/pitch the system writes back into
TransformComponent.rotation each frame. Round-tripped through
saves so a Free camera resumes facing the same direction.

members.name: targetYaw
members.doc:
Target yaw/pitch — input delta updates these every frame; the
visible yaw/pitch lerps toward them. Hidden + runtime-only so
they don't get saved (we resynchronise from yaw/pitch on load).

members.name: targetsInit
members.doc: false until first frame seeds targets from yaw/pitch

types.name: CameraShakeComponent
types.doc:
Trauma-based camera shake (Squirrel Eiserloh GDC pattern). Attach to
the camera entity; CameraShakeSystem decays trauma every frame and
writes the resulting offsets into the runtime fields, which
CameraSystem folds into the camera's view matrix on assembly.

members.name: trauma
members.doc:
Current trauma level. 0 = no shake, 1 = max. Decays toward 0 at
traumaDecay per second. Gameplay code adds trauma via AddTrauma()
— exposed in the inspector so designers can preview the feel.

members.name: maxOffsetPosition
members.doc:
Maximum positional amplitude in world units. Effective shake is
trauma² × maxOffset so most of the budget kicks in past 0.5.

members.name: maxRotationAngle
members.doc:
Maximum angular amplitude in degrees (small yaw/pitch/roll
perturbations layered on top of the camera's orientation).

members.name: noiseFrequency
members.doc:
How rapidly the shake direction flips. 25 Hz matches typical
hand-held-camera feel; lower for ground-rumble, higher for jitter.

members.name: noiseSeed
members.doc:
Deterministic seed. Two shake components with identical seeds
produce identical motion — bump for variety across cameras.

members.name: currentPositionOffset
members.doc:
Runtime — written by CameraShakeSystem each frame, read by
CameraSystem when assembling the active view matrix. Rotation
offsets are stored in radians as (pitch, yaw, roll) for direct
composition with the camera basis.

members.name: AddTrauma
members.doc: Additive — multiple explosions stack until the cap.
